content.content:
1	# レビューの依頼: git@github.com:akm/claude-plugins.git の docs/replace-kunyomi-literal-terms-135 (incremental)
2	
3	このファイルは review-triage プラグインの `review-request` スキルが生成した依頼文である。レビュアはこの依頼文だけを読んで作業し、結果を「出力様式」のとおり `/Users/akima/workspace/claude-plugins/tmp/review-20261025-2224-docs-replace-kunyomi-literal-terms-135-2-code-review-opus.yaml` に書き出す。依頼文の作り方と各節の理由の正本は review-triage スキルの `references/review-request.md` — レビュアが読む必要は無い。
4	
5	## 対象
6	
7	- リポジトリ: git@github.com:akm/claude-plugins.git (作業ツリー: `/Users/akima/workspace/claude-plugins`)
8	- 作業ツリーの扱い: 共有
9	- ブランチ: `docs/replace-kunyomi-literal-terms-135`
10	- 差分の範囲: `580c41a..8b6660a`
11	- scope: incremental — 前回の HEAD `580c41a` からの増分。増分の外は、増分が壊した場合のみ報告する
12	
13	## 作業ツリーの扱い
14	
15	「対象」の節の「作業ツリーの扱い」の値 (「共有」か「使い捨て」) によって、作業ツリーを変えてよい範囲が変わる。値に合う方の規則に従う。**どちらの値でも、指摘を見つけても直さない。** 直すかどうかは受け取る側が判断する。
16	
17	**「共有」のとき — 読み取り専用を厳守する。** 「対象」の節の作業ツリーは、依頼した側が作業している作業ツリーそのものである。
18	
19	- ファイルの編集・作成・削除をしない。git の状態 (HEAD・作業ツリー・インデックス・ブランチ) を変えない。
20	- 例外は出力先の 1 ファイル (`/Users/akima/workspace/claude-plugins/tmp/review-20261025-2224-docs-replace-kunyomi-literal-terms-135-2-code-review-opus.yaml`) だけ。他のファイルを作らない。
21	- レビューの前後で HEAD と作業ツリーが不変であることを確認して報告する。
22	
23	**「使い捨て」のとき — 複製の中でだけ変えてよい。** 「対象」の節の作業ツリーは、このレビューのためだけに作ったリポジトリの複製で、レビューが終わると削除される。
24	
25	- 確認のための変更 (ファイルを作る・変える・消す) は、この複製の中でだけしてよい。変えたものを戻さなくてよい。
26	- 逐語引用は、変える前の内容 (依頼の `head` のコミットにある内容) から取る。自分が変えたファイルから引かない。
27	- 一時ファイルも複製の中に作る (`/tmp` や環境変数 `TMPDIR` が指すディレクトリに作らない)。
28	- Bash のコマンドはサンドボックス (Claude Code の機能で、コマンドによるファイルの書き込みやネットワークの接続を、OS の仕組みで制限して実行するもの) の中で動く。次の 2 つは止められることがあるので、ほかの書き方があればそちらを選ぶ。
29	  - プロセス置換 (`diff <(コマンド) <(コマンド)` のように、コマンドの出力を一時的なファイルとして渡す書き方)。渡されるファイル `/dev/fd/<番号>` の読み取りが止められる。出力を複製の中のファイルに書いてから、そのファイルを渡す。
30	  - localhost の socket の bind (手元でポートを開いて待ち受けること)。利用者の設定で許されていなければ止められる。テストのランナーが、プラグインの読み込みなどで行うことがある (pytest のプラグインで起きた例がある)。localhost を使わない実行の方法 (unittest で書いたテストなら、pytest ではなく `python3 -m unittest`) があれば、そちらを選ぶ。
31	- 複製と出力先の外は変えない。
32	- HEAD を動かしたら (コマンド `git checkout`・`git reset`・`git commit` などで)、調べ続ける前に依頼の `head` (「対象」の節の差分の範囲の、`..` の右側のコミット) に戻す。複製の HEAD は detached HEAD (ブランチではなくコミットを直接指す状態) で、remote は設定されていない。結果を書き出したら、HEAD が依頼の `head` にあることを確認して報告する。
33	
34	## 呼ぶ skill・effort・モデル
35	
36	- skill: `code-review` / effort: `high` / モデル: `opus` — **この値で呼ぶ。** 自分で別の値を選ばない。effort が空なら、その skill は effort を受け取らない (`ce-code-review` など) ということで、値を補わない。`ce-code-review` はモデルの指定も適用されない — その場合のモデルは記録に残す名前であって、渡そうとしない。
37	- **報告に、skill を実際に呼んだか (呼んだ / 呼ばずに自分で読んだ) と、実際に渡した effort とモデルを含める。** 受け取る側はこの報告を上の指定と突き合わせる。
38	
39	## 検証の前払い (すべての指摘に必須)
40	
41	- evidence には次のいずれかを含める。どちらも含められない指摘は confidence を low にする。
42	  - 実行した確認 — コマンドと出力の要点、またはプローブ・ミューテーションの手順と結果
43	    (作業ツリーの扱いが「共有」なら、実施後は必ず revert し、作業ツリーが不変であることを確認して報告する。
44	    「使い捨て」なら revert しなくてよい。どちらも節「作業ツリーの扱い」の規則に従う)
45	  - 対象箇所の逐語引用 (行番号つき)。矛盾の主張なら、矛盾する 2 箇所の両方を引く
46	- 「〜の可能性がある」「余地がある」という形の主張には、それを実際に起こす入力・状態を 1 つ添える。
47	- テスト・検査の不在を主張する指摘 (「この入力のテストが無い」「この分岐が実行されていない」)
48	  は、その入力を実際に通して報告が出ないことを確かめてから出す。確かめられなければ
49	  confidence を low にする。テスト関数名の列挙や grep だけで結論しない — 別名のテストが
50	  同じ分岐を踏んでいることがある。
51	
52	## 報告しない条件と residual
53	
54	報告しない条件 (トリアージで却下される種類):
55	
56	- 壊れる入力・状態を具体に挙げられない一般的懸念
57	- 既存の関門 (テスト関数名・検査項目名で挙げられるもの) が、被害が出る前に検出する欠陥 (被害が起きたことが目に見えるだけのものは含まない)
58	- 対象そのものより大きい防御・再現の仕掛けを要求する指摘
59	- プロセスの遵守が diff から証明できない、という種類の観察
60	- 整理・統一の好み (放置して壊れるものが無いもの)。リファクタ提案は 1 件まで、その旨を明記して
61	
62	上に当たるが捨てるには惜しいものは、findings に入れず、末尾の residual リストに
63	1 行ずつだけ書く (id 無し・summary のみ)。判断の材料は残すが、指摘としては数えない。
64	
65	## 出力様式
66	
67	出力先: `/Users/akima/workspace/claude-plugins/tmp/review-20261025-2224-docs-replace-kunyomi-literal-terms-135-2-code-review-opus.yaml` — **この 1 ファイルだけ。** 名前を変えない。出力先のディレクトリが無ければ作る。コミットしない。
68	
69	次の構造に厳密に従う。**ここに無いキーを足さない。** 足したい情報があれば `attrs` (トップレベル・指摘の両方にある) に入れる。受け取る側は様式を確かめ、様式に無いキーがあれば判定を始めずに差し戻す。
70	
71	```yaml
72	skill: code-review
73	model: opus
74	level: "high"
75	run_id: "20261025-2224-docs-replace-kunyomi-literal-terms-135-2-code-review-opus"
76	scope: incremental
77	base: "580c41a"
78	head: "8b6660a"
79	date: "2026-10-25"
80	attrs: {}
81	findings:
82	  - id: 1
83	    file: path/to/file.md
84	    line: 12
85	    summary: "1〜2 文の要旨"
86	    evidence: "検証の前払いの節のとおり"
87	    attrs:
88	      severity: P2
89	      confidence: high
90	residual: []
91	```
92	
93	| キー | 内容 |
94	| --- | --- |
95	| `skill` / `model` / `level` / `scope` / `base` / `head` / `date` | 上に埋めた値のまま書く。`level` は指定された effort。`head` は作業開始時の HEAD の短縮 SHA と一致すること |
96	| `run_id` | `review-request` が識別子で埋める。上に埋めた値のまま書く。受け取る側は記録の `runs[].run_id` にそのまま写す |
97	| `attrs` (トップレベル) | 上に挙げたキー以外に残したい情報 (PR 番号など)。無ければ `{}` |
98	| `findings[].id` | 1 からの連番 |
99	| `findings[].file` / `line` | 指摘の位置。`line` は不明なら省略 |
100	| `findings[].summary` | 1〜2 文の要旨 |
101	| `findings[].evidence` | 「検証の前払い」の節のとおり |
102	| `findings[].attrs` | レビューが付けた属性 (`severity` / `confidence` など) をそのまま。無い属性を補完しない |
103	| `residual` | 「報告しない条件」に当たるが残す 1 行メモの列。無ければ `[]` |
104	
105	注意:
106	
107	- 指摘が 0 件なら `findings: []` と書く。キーを省かない。件数の集計は書かない (読み手が計算する)。
108	- 行内コメント (` #` 以降) を書かない。YAML は「半角スペース + `#`」以降をコメントとして取り除くので、値が警告なく切り詰められる。値に `#` を含めるときは引用符で囲む。
109	- 指摘の取捨は「報告しない条件」に従い、それ以外は全件書く。修正はしない。
110	- 書き出したら、節「作業ツリーの扱い」の、値に合う方の確認をして報告する。

content.text: Plan updated: step 2 of 3 is in progress.

Review target: `8b6660a..b8f2879`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text: Plan updated: step 2 of 3 is in progress.

Review target: `f2362c2..816929b`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text: Plan updated: step 2 of 3 is in progress.

Review target: `621e3b5..be3d6c6`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text: Plan updated: step 2 of 3 is in progress.

Review target: `be3d6c6..5167660`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured

content.text: Plan updated: step 2 of 3 is in progress.

Review target: `c86a49c..31eadb6`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line

wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.

path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name

that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the

is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

content.text: Plan updated: step 2 of 3 is in progress.

Review target: `9791c89..3260710`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

content.text: Plan updated: step 2 of 3 is in progress.

Review target: `df22399..d29b9e7`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Review target: `d29b9e7..b434d87`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.

host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings

Review target: `df22399..b434d87`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

+// 別のパスに変わる。埋め込む値と展開させる変数を、引用符の種類で判別できる
-// -summary-command は生成時に決めた値を焼き込む。実行時の $0 から組み立てない —
+// -summary-command は生成時に決めた値を埋め込む。実行時の $0 から組み立てない —
-// 解決しないので、PATH 上などに張ったリンク経由で起動すると基準がリンクの置き場に
-// なり、その隣に別の置き場があるとそちらを検査して成功を返す (基準が検査対象から
-// 切り離される点で、絶対パスを焼き込む案を退けたのと同じ種類の問題)。リンクを辿ってから

+// なり、その隣に別の記録のディレクトリがあるとそちらを検査して成功を返す (基準が検査対象から

+# リンクのあるディレクトリが基準になり、その隣に別の記録のディレクトリがあるとそちらを検査してしまう。

# CLAUDE.md

このリポジトリの文書 (Markdown) を書く・直すときの規則。

## 文書の表現

文書を読んだ人間やエージェントは、そこで使われている語をそのまま新しい文書・コミットメッセージ・記録に複製する。規範文書が不自然な語彙を供給すると、それがリポジトリ全体に広がる。次の 3 原則に従って書く。

1. **説明のない省略や比喩、安直な英語の翻訳は使わない。** ただし日本語圏のエンジニアに通じる言葉なら許容する。
2. **正しい英語を翻訳するのではなく、日本語の文章として正しい文章を書く。**
3. **専門用語やコンテキスト依存の造語は、初出の際にコンテキストを把握していない人間向けに説明する文を添える。** 文章として不自然な場合は括弧などを使う。

網羅的な避ける表現の一覧は作らない。列挙を検査の範囲にすると、一覧に無いものが検査されないまま残る。例として一覧を作ることは許容する。そのときは、一覧が例であって範囲ではないことを一覧に書く。一覧に無い表現も、この 3 原則に照らして判断する。

言い換えを決めた語と、使い続けると決めた語は、ファイル `.claude/akm-claude-plugins/wording-guard/terms.toml` に例として記録している (様式の正本はファイル [wording-guard/skills/wording-guard/references/terms.md](wording-guard/skills/wording-guard/references/terms.md))。

例外: トリアージ記録 (現行のディレクトリ `tmp/review-triages/` と、過去にコミットした `docs/review-triage/`) は、レビュー指摘を逐語で引用するため書き換えない。

経緯は [#35](https://github.com/akm/claude-plugins/issues/35) と [#89](https://github.com/akm/claude-plugins/issues/89) を参照。

- [古いブランチの整理](abandoned-branch-fix-a1-exemption-label-43.md) — main 以外は消した。main に無いコミットはタグ archive/* に残した。#43・#44 は main から作り直す
- [PR #49 review-triage 0.9.0 の未実施項目](review-triage-0-9-followups.md) — 通し確認は未実施。Go は 1.25.4 で検証。cross-model は許可を得てから
- [review-loop 実装の通し確認](review-loop-impl-verification-pending.md) — #66〜#85・#91 (#86、0.20.0) はマージ済み。#65・#70・#79・#81・#87・#88 は未解決
- [「最終確認」と呼ばない](avoid-term-saishu-kakunin.md) — 収束後の全量レビューは採択があれば直して増分に戻る。言い換えは「収束後の全量レビュー」(#71)
- [コメントの訂正は書き換えで](edit-comment-instead-of-correction.md) — 自分が投稿した Issue / PR のコメントは、訂正のコメントを足さず元を書き換える
- [「許させない」と書かない](avoid-yurusasenai.md) — 許す の使役形は不自然。「許可させない」「許可させず」と書く
- [文書の相互参照の解き方](doc-cross-reference-direction.md) — ファイル内は片方を正本に (無理なら共通の節)。ファイル間は参照される側にまとめる
- [ワーカーは端末のタブで起動する](launch-worker-in-terminal-tab.md) — 承認を得て run_in_terminal で起動。Bash ツールでは起動しない
- [Closes #N が効かない](closes-keyword-not-applied.md) — マージ後に Issue が開いたままなら、PR への参照を付けて手で閉じる
- [「周回」「回 1」と書かない](avoid-shuukai-kai-n.md) — #87 で不自然と記録済み。新しい文章では「review-loop の実行」「1 回目」
- [別の作業ツリーへのレビュー結果の書き出し](review-output-other-worktree.md) — hook が止めるので自分の tmp/ に書き、cp のコマンドを渡す
- [並べてレビューするときの作業ツリー](subagent-review-worktree-isolation.md) — ブランチごとに worktree を作り、メインで checkout しないよう依頼に書く。マージまで残す
- [review-triage の各スキルを毎回呼ぶ](invoke-review-triage-skills-each-time.md) — 判定は毎回 review-triage を呼ぶ。依頼文は review-request で作り、人間が別セッションで走らせる
- [方向・位置の比喩で関係を書かない](avoid-direction-metaphor.md) — 「逆向きの問題」「〜側」は何がどう違うかを書かない。比喩を使わずに書く
- [ほかのプロジェクト名を公開の場に書かない](no-other-project-names-in-public.md) — Issue・PR には「あるプロジェクト」と書く。番号・リンクも書かない
- [レビュアがメインの .git を書き換えうる](reviewer-may-rewrite-main-repo.md) — 結果を受け取ったら git branch -v と reflog を見る。git を呼ぶテストは GIT_DIR などを消す
- [修正のコミットの前に言い回しを確かめる](wording-check-before-fix-commit.md) — 変えた Markdown・Go のコメント・コミットメッセージを wording-guard (--stdin) と目視で。#110 で毎回 1 回遅れて指摘された
- [PR #115 はレビューを止めて push 済み](pr115-review-loop-stopped.md) — 2026-10-18 に ready for review。次はマージ後に別ブランチで U1。計画で決めなかった指摘は Open Questions の一覧
- [判断は自分で決めず尋ねる・問いはまとめる](ask-rather-than-decide-batch-questions.md) — 問いの回数より確認漏れを避けることを優先する。設計でも問いの削減を目標にしない。多く、利用者からも質問が出そうなら一つずつ地の文で。途中で選ばれた「問題ごとにまとめる」もある
- [「列」ではなく「配列」](say-hairetsu-not-retsu.md) — array は「配列」と書く。「名前の列」→「名前の配列」。表の列・文字列は対象外
- [用語に読点を入れない](no-comma-in-terms.md) — 長い用語も 1 続きで書く。読点を含むと用語に見えない (PR #115 の計画で指摘)
- [条件は略さず文で書く](write-conditions-in-full.md) — 「X が ask で Y を選んだら」と並べず、どの対象の・どの場面で・誰が何をするかを書く (P3 の説明で指摘)。説明のページは前提・問題・対処案・問いだけを端的に書き、経緯は書かず、問題は今の状態として書く。「合っていない」には、どうあるべきかの決まりを添える (P13 で指摘)
- [依存の矢印は「使う」](dependency-arrow-uses.md) — 根本が使うもの・矢じりが使われるもの。「使われる」と書かない。mermaid では上下の並びを保つため、描いた後に矢じりを付け替える
- [説明の図に書かれる場所を描く](explainer-diagram-show-where-written.md) — 作るもの・Issue・PR・Status を参加者にし、前提にやり取りの経路を表で書く。mermaid の `#9` は `#35;9`
- [issue-dispatch の U1 は終えた](issue-dispatch-u1-done.md) — 計画への反映の PR #119 はマージ済み。次は U2 (設定) から別のブランチで実装
- [issue-dispatch の U2 は PR #120](issue-dispatch-u2-pr120.md) — 設定の読み込み。PR #120 はマージ済み。単位ごとに PR
- [issue-dispatch の U3 は PR #121](issue-dispatch-u3-pr121.md) — ファイルの種類。PR #121 はマージ済み。決めたことは file-kinds.md が持つ
- [issue-dispatch の U4 は PR #122](issue-dispatch-u4-pr122.md) — gh の実行の関数・偽の gh・固定データ。PR #122 はマージ済み。後の単位は fake-gh と expect_json=True を使う
- [issue-dispatch の U5 は PR #123](issue-dispatch-u5-pr123.md) — 記録の読み書き。PR #123 はマージ済み。
- [issue-dispatch の U6 は PR #124](issue-dispatch-u6-pr124.md) — リポジトリの設定の読み方。PR #124 はマージ済み。名前の形は使える文字だけで決める
- [issue-dispatch の U7 前半は PR #125](issue-dispatch-u7a-pr125.md) — 参照の正規化と Project。PR #125 はマージ済み。後半 (Issue と PR) は別のブランチで。GraphQL は --input - の本文で渡す
- [issue-dispatch の U7 後半は PR #126](issue-dispatch-u7b-pr126.md) — Issue と PR の読み書き・issue-format.md。PR #126 はマージ済み。次は U8 (コメント)
- [issue-dispatch の U8 は PR #127](issue-dispatch-u8-pr127.md) — コメントの先頭行・一覧・投稿。PR #127 はマージ済み。次は U9 (セッション)
- [issue-dispatch の U9 は PR #128](issue-dispatch-u9-pr128.md) — セッションの識別・規約の名前・messaging.md。PR #128 はマージ済み。次は U10 (宣言)
- [issue-dispatch の U10 は PR #129](issue-dispatch-u10-pr129.md) — 宣言の様式・検査・更新の種類・競合の可能性。PR #129 はマージ済み。次は U11 (資源)
- [issue-dispatch の U11 は PR #130](issue-dispatch-u11-pr130.md) — 資源の属性と契機ごとの判断・resources.md。PR #130 はマージ済み。次は U12 (スナップショットと差分)
- [「印」ではなく「フラグ」](say-flag-not-shirushi.md) — データに付ける目印は「フラグ」と書く。「印」は矢印などの字面の意味だけ (U12 の説明ページで指摘)
- [issue-dispatch の U12 は PR #131](issue-dispatch-u12-pr131.md) — スナップショットと差分・observation.md。PR #131 はマージ済み。欠けは引き継ぐ (案 D) か partial で比べない。次は U13 (項目の状態)
- [issue-dispatch の U13 前半は PR #132](issue-dispatch-u13a-pr132.md) — 項目の状態の導出・work check / held・flow.md。PR #132 はマージ済み。案 3・7・8・9 は後半
- [issue-dispatch の U13 後半は PR #133](issue-dispatch-u13b-pr133.md) — ターンで行うことの導出・blocked-by remove・flow.md の残り。PR #133 はマージ済み。次は U14 (待機)
- [issue-dispatch の U14 は PR #134](issue-dispatch-u14-pr134.md) — 待機 (wait・wait-assignment・wait-decision・wait.pid)。PR #134 はマージ済み。次は U15 (判定)
- [issue-dispatch の U15 前半は PR #136](issue-dispatch-u15a-judge.md) — 判定 (judge・declaration judge)。#136 マージ済み。doc-dag の相互参照は PR #137 (マージ待ち)。後半は別ブランチ
- [語の選び方の優先順](prefer-sino-japanese-terms.md) — 識別子・正式な用語・手順書に書かれうるものは原語のまま → 浸透したカタカナ語 → 二字漢語 → 訓読みの直訳は避ける。既存の文書は Issue #135 で洗い出してから直す
- [#135 の進み具合](issue-135-kunyomi-progress.md) — PR を 4 つに分ける。PR1 は #138 でマージ済み。PR2 は #139 でマージ済み。PR3 は 3a (review-loop) と 3b に分けた。3a は #140 でマージ済み (df22399)。3b は #141 でマージ済み (f98cb40)。PR4 (比喩) は 4a (review-triage 以外) のレビュー中。4b (review-triage) は 4a のマージ後

# CLAUDE.md

このリポジトリの文書 (Markdown) を書く・直すときの規則。

## 文書の表現

文書を読んだ人間やエージェントは、そこで使われている語をそのまま新しい文書・コミットメッセージ・記録に複製する。規範文書が不自然な語彙を供給すると、それがリポジトリ全体に広がる。次の 3 原則に従って書く。

1. **説明のない省略や比喩、安直な英語の翻訳は使わない。** ただし日本語圏のエンジニアに通じる言葉なら許容する。
2. **正しい英語を翻訳するのではなく、日本語の文章として正しい文章を書く。**
3. **専門用語やコンテキスト依存の造語は、初出の際にコンテキストを把握していない人間向けに説明する文を添える。** 文章として不自然な場合は括弧などを使う。

網羅的な避ける表現の一覧は作らない。列挙を検査の範囲にすると、一覧に無いものが検査されないまま残る。例として一覧を作ることは許容する。そのときは、一覧が例であって範囲ではないことを一覧に書く。一覧に無い表現も、この 3 原則に照らして判断する。

言い換えを決めた語と、使い続けると決めた語は、ファイル `.claude/akm-claude-plugins/wording-guard/terms.toml` に例として記録している (様式の正本はファイル [wording-guard/skills/wording-guard/references/terms.md](wording-guard/skills/wording-guard/references/terms.md))。

例外: トリアージ記録 (現行のディレクトリ `tmp/review-triages/` と、過去にコミットした `docs/review-triage/`) は、レビュー指摘を逐語で引用するため書き換えない。

経緯は [#35](https://github.com/akm/claude-plugins/issues/35) と [#89](https://github.com/akm/claude-plugins/issues/89) を参照。

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results
with `{level, findings}`. `findings` is at most 10 entries ranked
most-severe first; each entry has `file`, `line`, `summary`,
`short_summary` — the claim compressed to ≤60 characters, no rationale
or consequence clause — `failure_scenario`, and `category` — a short kebab-case slug for the angle
that produced it (`correctness`, `simplification`, `efficiency`,
`reuse`, `altitude`, `conventions`, or a more specific slug like
`test-coverage` when one fits better) — plus `verdict` when a verify pass
produced one. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most severe. If
nothing survives, call it with an empty array. Do not also print
the findings as text, and do not create or publish an artifact of the review -
the tool call is the report.


## If findings are fixed later

Whenever reported findings get fixed later in this session - the user asks you
to fix them, or later work fixes them incidentally - you MUST call ReportFindings again with the same findings, each
carrying an `outcome`: `fixed`, `no_change_needed` (the finding was wrong or
already handled), or `skipped` (real but not applied). Do not repeat the
findings as text.
Make that call immediately after the fixes land, before any prose summary; the
host UI's per-finding status updates only from it, and without it the findings
stay marked unresolved.

PR4a (比喩の言い換え、review-triage 以外) の全量レビューを終えました。指摘は 0 件、residual は 1 件で、結果を `tmp/review-20261027-0005-docs-replace-metaphors-135-1-code-review-opus.yaml` に書き出しました。様式どおりの YAML として読めることも確認しました。

**依頼の指定との対応**
- skill: `code-review` は Skill ツールで実際に呼びました。引数は `high f98cb40..f1fba73` で、渡した effort は `high` です。
- モデル: `code-review` はモデルを引数で受け取らないため、渡していません。このセッションのモデル Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) で実行しました。
- 作業ツリー: 開始時と終了時の両方で HEAD は `f1fba73`、`git status --porcelain` は空でした。書いたのは結果のファイルだけです。

**確認したこと**
- 差分 (64 ファイル・164 行) を単語単位ですべて読みました。主な置き換えは次の 3 種類で、どれも前後の文脈と照らして意味が保たれていました。
  - 「〜側」を、指すもの (呼び出し元・関数・プロセス・正本の記述など) か「方」にした
  - 「狂わせる」を「影響を受ける」にした
  - 「安全側」を「見落としを出さないため」にした
- 実行時のメッセージや出力の変更はありません。変わったのは、コメント・docstring・文書だけです。
- テストは 5 つのプラグイン (commit-rules-guard・pr-teeth・wording-guard・work-log-gh-comment・issue-dispatch) で、すべて成功しました。
- 用語ファイルの様式の検査は通りました。新しく登録した避ける語「前払い」「狂う」(活用形を含む) が error になることも確認しました。
- 版を上げた 7 つのプラグインは、このブランチで中身を変えたプラグインと一致しています。

**residual (1 件)**
- review-triage の外にある `CONCEPTS.md` (102・112・117・122 行) とルートの `README.md:177` に、review-loop の用語「作業側」が残っています。PR4b で「作業側」を言い換えるときは、この 5 か所もそろえる必要があります。

content.text:
Review target: `a8defa2..ef4f94a`

`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)
